ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2.
The sequence s has exactly n minus 1 entries.
Each entry of s is either plus 1 or minus 1.
The tuple a is a permutation of {1, 2, ..., n}, so all entries are distinct and each integer from 1 to n appears exactly once.
The inequality si times (a(i+1) - ai) greater than 0 means ai+1 is greater than ai when si is plus 1, and ai+1 is less than ai when si is minus 1.
The constraint must hold for every index i from 1 to n minus 1.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n at least 2, among all length n minus 1 sequences of plus or minus 1, determine exactly which sign patterns maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs.
quantifier_order: First fix an integer n with n at least 2.
Then range over all sign sequences s of length n minus 1.
For a given s, count all permutations a of {1, 2, ..., n} satisfying the adjacent sign constraints for every i from 1 to n minus 1.
Finally, for each n, identify which sequences s maximize this count.

payload.proof_nl:
Let e_i be the i-th standard basis vector of length m (so e_i has a 1 in position i and 0 elsewhere). For a sign string t, define c_t(i)=Total(T_t(e_i)). Since U, D, and Total are linear, T_t is linear, hence for every x=(x_1,...,x_m),
Total(T_t(x))=sum_{i=1}^m c_t(i)x_i.
So it is enough to understand the coefficients c_t(i).

For t=(t_1,...,t_r) and indices i,j, call a sequence p_0,p_1,...,p_r an admissible t-chain from i to j if p_0=i, p_r=j, 1<=p_k<=m+k for each k, and for each k:
- if t_k=+1, then p_{k-1}<p_k;
- if t_k=-1, then p_{k-1}>=p_k.
I claim that T_t(e_i)_j is exactly the number of admissible t-chains from i to j.

This is proved by induction on r. For r=1, if t=(+1), then U(e_i)_j=1 exactly when i<j and 0 otherwise, so it counts one-step admissible chains. If t=(-1), then D(e_i)_j=1 exactly when i>=j and 0 otherwise, so it again counts one-step admissible chains.

For the induction step, suppose the claim is true for a sign string t of length r, and let t' be obtained by appending one more sign. If the new sign is +1, then for each j,
T_{t'}(e_i)_j=U(T_t(e_i))_j=sum_{h=1}^{j-1} T_t(e_i)_h.
By the induction hypothesis, this counts exactly the admissible t-chains from i to h, summed over all h<j; that is exactly the number of admissible t'-chains from i to j. If the new sign is -1, then similarly
T_{t'}(e_i)_j=D(T_t(e_i))_j=sum_{h=j}^{m+r} T_t(e_i)_h,
which counts exactly the admissible t'-chains from i to j. Thus the claim holds for all r.

Therefore c_t(i)=Total(T_t(e_i)) is the number of admissible t-chains starting at i, with arbitrary endpoint.

Now let a_i=c_{Alt_r^+}(i). Because the first sign of Alt_r^+ is +1, every admissible Alt_r^+-chain starting at i+1 is also admissible starting at i: indeed the only condition involving the start is p_0<p_1, and i+1<p_1 implies i<p_1. Hence a_i>=a_{i+1}.

This inclusion is strict for every i<m. Consider the chain defined by
p_0=i,
p_1=i+1,
and for k>=2,
p_k=1 if k is even, and p_k=m+k if k is odd.
This satisfies the alternating conditions +,-,+,-,..., so it is an admissible Alt_r^+-chain starting at i. But it is not admissible starting at i+1, because its first step would require i+1<p_1=i+1, which is false. Therefore
a_1>a_2>...>a_m.

Next let b_i=c_{Alt_r^-}(i). I claim that b_i=a_{m+1-i}. Take any admissible Alt_r^+-chain p_0=i,p_1,...,p_r and define
q_k=m+k+1-p_k  for 0<=k<=r.
Then q_0=m+1-i and 1<=q_k<=m+k for every k. Also, Alt_r^- is obtained from Alt_r^+ by flipping every sign, and the inequalities transform correctly:
- if the k-th sign of Alt_r^+ is +1, then p_{k-1}<p_k, so
  q_{k-1}-q_k=(m+k-p_{k-1})-(m+k+1-p_k)=p_k-p_{k-1}-1>=0,
  hence q_{k-1}>=q_k;
- if the k-th sign of Alt_r^+ is -1, then p_{k-1}>=p_k, so
  q_{k-1}-q_k=p_k-p_{k-1}-1<=-1,
  hence q_{k-1}<q_k.
So q is an admissible Alt_r^--chain starting at m+1-i. The same transformation is its own inverse, so this is a bijection. Hence b_i=a_{m+1-i}.

Now define
F_+(x)=Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(x)),
F_-(x)=Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(x)).
By linearity and the identities above,
F_+(x)=sum_{i=1}^m a_i x_i,
F_-(x)=sum_{i=1}^m a_{m+1-i} x_i.
Therefore
F_+(x)-F_-(x)=sum_{i=1}^m (a_i-a_{m+1-i})x_i.
Pairing the terms with indices i and m+1-i gives
F_+(x)-F_-(x)=sum_{i=1}^{floor(m/2)} (a_i-a_{m+1-i})(x_i-x_{m+1-i}).
Because a_1>a_2>...>a_m, each coefficient a_i-a_{m+1-i} in this sum is positive.

If x is nonnegative and nonincreasing, then x_i>=x_{m+1-i} for every i<=floor(m/2). Hence every term in the last sum is >=0, so F_+(x)>=F_-(x). If x is nonconstant, then x_1>x_m, and since a_1>a_m, the term with i=1 is >0; therefore F_+(x)>F_-(x).

If x is nonnegative and nondecreasing, then x_i<=x_{m+1-i} for every i<=floor(m/2). Hence every term in the last sum is <=0, so F_+(x)<=F_-(x), i.e. F_-(x)>=F_+(x). If x is nonconstant, then x_1<x_m, so the term with i=1 is <0; therefore F_+(x)<F_-(x).

This is exactly the stated lemma.

domain_restrictions: m and r are positive integers.
The generic vector y has length ell, where ell is a positive integer.
The sign string t has length r and each entry is either plus one or minus one.
Empty sums are defined to be zero.
x has length m.
All entries of x are nonnegative.
In the first comparison, x is nonincreasing, meaning its entries do not increase as the index increases.
In the second comparison, x is nondecreasing, meaning its entries do not decrease as the index increases.
The strict inequality clauses apply only when x is nonconstant, meaning not all entries of x are equal.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: With m and r fixed as positive integers, define U, D, T_t, Total, and the two alternating sign strings as stated. Then every nonnegative weakly decreasing vector x of length m satisfies that the total after the plus-starting alternating composition is at least the total after the minus-starting alternating composition, and the inequality is strict when x is not constant. Likewise, every nonnegative weakly increasing vector x of length m satisfies the reverse inequality, again strict when x is not constant.
quantifier_order: For each positive integer m and each positive integer r, the operators and sign strings are defined in terms of these fixed parameters.
For every vector y of length ell, U(y), D(y), and Total(y) are defined using the given formulas, with empty sums interpreted as zero.
For every sign string t of length r, T_t is obtained by applying U or D successively according to the signs in t.
For every vector x of length m that is nonnegative and nonincreasing, Total applied to T_Alt_r_plus of x is at least Total applied to T_Alt_r_minus of x.
If such an x is nonconstant, the previous inequality is strict.
For every vector x of length m that is nonnegative and nondecreasing, Total applied to T_Alt_r_minus of x is at least Total applied to T_Alt_r_plus of x.
If such an x is nonconstant, the previous inequality is strict.

payload.statement_nl: Fix positive integers m and r. Define U, D, T_t, Total, Alt_r^+, and Alt_r^- exactly as follows: if y=(y_1,...,y_ell), then U(y) and D(y) are length ell+1 vectors given by U(y)_j = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} y_i and D(y)_j = sum_{i=j}^{ell} y_i for 1 <= j <= ell+1, with empty sums equal to 0; for a sign string t=(t_1,...,t_r), T_t(x) is obtained by applying U or D successively according to the signs; Alt_r^+=(+1,-1,+1,-1,...) and Alt_r^-=(-1,+1,-1,+1,...) have length r; and Total(y) is the sum of the entries of y. If x is a nonnegative nonincreasing vector of length m, then Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(x)) >= Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(x)), with strict inequality if x is nonconstant. If x is a nonnegative nondecreasing vector of length m, then Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(x)) >= Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(x)), with strict inequality if x is nonconstant.

dependency_assessment.notes: Proof is self-contained relative to the lemma statement and operator definitions.

detailed_findings.finding: The induction identifying T_t(e_i)_j with the number of admissible t-chains is correct and matches the U/D recurrence exactly.
The proof does not use nonnegativity of x, so it actually proves a slightly stronger comparison for all weakly monotone x; this is harmless and not semantic drift.

result_payload.reason: The proof is complete and internally coherent. It correctly expresses Total∘T_t as a linear functional on x, identifies the coefficients via an induction that counts admissible chains, proves strict monotonicity of the coefficient sequence for Alt_r^+ by an inclusion-plus-witness argument, derives the Alt_r^- coefficients by an explicit involutive reflection bijection, and then finishes by pairing symmetric indices to compare the two totals for monotone x. The strictness arguments for nonconstant weakly monotone x are also valid. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used.
